  2. 5. It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances, without the concurrence of the legislative council, during an emergency. The life of such an ordinance was 6 months.

Indian Councils Act, 1892

  1. 1. It introduced indirect elections.
  2. 2. It permitted discussions on financial matters, and allowed members to question the executive, enhancing accountability.

Indian Councils Act, 1909

  • Also known as Morley-Minto Reforms (Lord Morley - Secretary of State and Lord Minto - Viceroy of India).
  1. 1. Increased the size of the legislative councils, both Central and Provincial. The no. of members in the central legislative council was raised from 16 to 60.
  2. 2. Members: Official majority in central legislative council and non-official majority in Provincial legislative council.
  3. 3. It provided for the association of Indians with Executive Councils of the Viceroys and Governor (Satyendra Prasad Sinha was the 1st Indian to join, later appointed as the Law member).
  4. 4. It introduced Separate Electorate for Muslims (System of Communal Representation), i.e., Muslim members were elected by Muslim voters (Lord Minto: Father of Communal Electorate).

Government of India Act, 1919

  • Also known as Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Montagu - Secretary of State for India and Lord Chelmsford - Viceroy of India).
  1. 1. Dyarchy introduced in provinces.
  2. 2. Classified all the subjects of administration into the central subjects and the provincial subjects. Provincial Subjects were further divided into two parts: Transferred and Reserved subjects.
Transferred subjects (Governor General not responsible): Public health, Education, Local Self government, Agriculture, etc.
Reserved subjects (Governor General responsible): Police, Administration of justice, Prison, Land revenue, Finance, etc.
  1. 3. It introduced Bicameralism and direct elections in the country for the 1st time, consisting of an Upper House (Council of State) and a Lower House (Legislative Assembly).
  2. 4. It required that 3 of the 6 members of the Viceroy's executive council (other than the Commander-in-Chief) were to be Indian.
  3. 5. It created a new office of the High Commissioner for India in London and transferred to him some of the functions.
  4. 6. Public Service Commission was established and a Central Public Service Commission was set up in 1926 for recruiting civil servants.
  5. 7. It separated Provincial budget from central budget.
  6. 8. It extended the system of Separate Electorate for: Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.

Government of India Act, 1935

_(Enforced on: 1st April 1937)_

  1. 1. It abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced dyarchy at the Centre, provided Autonomy to the Centre.
  2. 2. It provided for the establishment of an All India Federation consisting of provinces and princely states as units.
  3. 3. It introduced bicameralism in 6 out of 11 provinces (Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces).
  4. 4. It reserved certain no. of seats for Scheduled Castes, women and labourers.
  5. 5. It extended adult franchise - Only 14% of total population had the right to vote.
  6. 6. Reserve Bank of India was established.
  7. 7. Federal Public Service Commission, Provincial Public Service Commission and Joint Public Service Commission were established.
  8. 8. Federal Court was set up in 1937.
  9. 9. Burma (now Myanmar) was separated from India.
  10. 10. The Act divided the powers between the Centre and units in three lists - Federal List (for Centre, with 59 items), Provincial List (for provinces, with 54 items) and the Concurrent List (for both, with 36 items).
  11. 11. Residuary powers were given to the Viceroy (Governor-General).
  12. 12. It abolished the council of 15 members.

Indian Independence Act, 1947

  1. 1. It ended the British rule in India and declared India as an independent and sovereign state from August 15, 1947.
  2. 2. Partition of India and creation of two independent dominions of India and Pakistan with the right to secede from the British Commonwealth was done.
  3. 3. It abolished the office of Viceroy and provided a Governor General, who was to be appointed by the British King on the advice of the dominion cabinet.
  4. 4. It abolished the office of the Secretary of State for India and transferred his functions to the Secretary of State for Commonwealth Affairs.
  5. 5. It proclaimed the lapse of British paramountcy over the Indian princely states and treaty relations with tribal areas from August 15, 1947.
  6. 6. It granted freedom to the Indian princely states either to join the Dominion of India or Dominion of Pakistan or to remain independent.
  7. 7. The Governor-General would have full power to assent to any bill in the name of His Majesty.
  8. 8. It designated the Governor-General of India and the provincial governors as constitutional (nominal) heads of the states.
  9. 9. It dropped the title of Emperor of India from the royal titles of the King of England.
  10. 10. It discontinued the appointment to civil services and reservation of posts by the secretary of state for India.
  11. 11. It is also known as the Partition plan / Mountbatten plan / June 3rd plan.

At the stroke of midnight of 14-15 August, 1947, the British rule came to an end.

  • 1st Governor General of Independent India: Mountbatten
  • 1st and last Indian Governor General: C. Rajagopalachari

  • Indian Independence Act 1947 (end of British rule, partition, dominion)
